texts: good. it fires as a rule over sky-cats with both season adjuncts on the molting; season names have no standard time term yet, so "late summer" and "early autumn" are recorded as plain symbols.
good. fireable whenever rule — each molting drops feathers, with the base of the cliff as the goal and the base linked to the cliff it belongs to.

good. the collectors, their link to Tessa Brae, the each-morning recurrence and the "fallen" property of every feather all land; only "during molting weeks" sits loosely, attaching a period kind rather than a stretch of time the reasoner can relate to anything.

bad: "sky-cat feathers" was welded into a single kind, so nothing records that the feathers come off sky-cats and the rule connects to nothing else you say about them — a part and its owner have to stay separate words. Rewrite with the ownership spelled out: "Ground feathers of sky-cats ward lanterns against wraiths." — the very next sentence's identical phrase happened to parse the right way, so the "of" wording is the reliable one.

mixed: the belief is recorded properly (the Keepers hold sky-cats sacred, without that making them sacred), but the "because" is dropped entirely — the reason clause becomes a general rule, and a rule offers no single happening for a causal link to point at. State the reason as one concrete happening instead: "The Keepers consider sky-cats sacred because a sky-cat's feather wards a lantern against wraiths." The general version of that claim already stands as its own sentence in this rule, so nothing is lost by narrowing it here.
good. "never" comes out as a flat denial that the Keepers harm any sky-cat, with the sky-cat kept inside the denial as required.
good. the hedge "sometimes" is carried as a reduced-strength claim rather than dropped, and the flight, the spires and the carried nightmoth all land.
